blog_summary: Adrian Colyer discusses the shift from traditional ORM-style patterns to event-driven architectures in cloud-native applications, particularly focusing on microservices and dataflow. He highlights the benefits of an event store (append-only storage) and event sourcing, which enable retrospective analysis and maintain business value by retaining transactional history. The blog emphasizes the challenges of event ordering and consistency, drawing parallels to consensus algorithms like Paxos and CRDTs. Colyer explores the relationship between CQRS and event sourcing, noting their limitations in achieving strong consistency. He introduces the idea of modeling microservices as nodes in a dataflow graph, akin to stream processing systems like Apache Flink or AWS Lambda, and suggests dynamic updates to the dataflow graph as a powerful agile platform. The post concludes by advocating for application-centric design with just-enough coordination to achieve causal+ consistency, while acknowledging the complexity of reasoning about consistency in distributed systems.
